label: Discovered the atomic nucleus
description: Rutherford made his epoch-making discovery of the atomic nucleus.

sources.quote: only a few months before had led him to his epoch-making discovery of the atomic nucleus

label: Bohr joined Rutherford's group in Manchester
description: Bohr joined the group working in Rutherford's laboratory in the early spring of 1912.

sources.quote: he kindly assented to my wish to join the group working in his laboratory when, in the early spring of 1912, I should have finished my studies in Cambridge

label: Rutherford prepared Radioactive Substances and Their Radiations
description: Rutherford was concentrating on the preparation of his great book.

sources.quote: Although Rutherford just at that time was concentrating on the preparation of his great book, Radioactive Substances and Their Radiations

label: Bohr sent draft of first paper to Rutherford
description: Bohr wrote to Rutherford enclosing a draft of his first paper on the quantum theory of atomic constitution.

sources.quote: When in March 1913 I wrote to Rutherford, enclosing a draft of my first paper on the quantum theory of atomic constitution

label: Rutherford accepted Cavendish professorship
description: Rutherford made the decision to accept the offer of the Cavendish professorship in Cambridge.

sources.quote: Rutherford also spoke about the great decision he had had to make in response to the offer of the Cavendish professorship in Cambridge left vacant by the retirement of J. J. Thomson.

label: Rutherford discovered artificial nuclear transmutations
description: Rutherford made his great new discovery of controlled, or so-called artificial, nuclear transmutations.

sources.quote: learned in more detail about his great new discovery of controlled, or so-called artificial, nuclear transmutations, by which he gave birth to what he liked to call ' modern Alchemy '

label: Rutherford published papers in Philosophical Magazine
description: Rutherford's famous papers containing the account of his fundamental discovery of controlled nuclear disintegrations.

sources.quote: In Rutherford's famous papers in the Philosophical Magazine, 1919, containing the account of his fundamental discovery of controlled nuclear disintegrations

label: Rutherford gave second Bakerian Lecture
description: Rutherford pointed out difficulties of interpreting alpha-ray emission in his second Bakerian Lecture.

sources.quote: Rutherford himself had as early as 1920 in his second Bakerian Lecture clearly pointed out the difficulties of interpreting cc-ray emission froin nuclei

label: Rutherford visited Copenhagen
description: Rutherford visited the Copenhagen Institute in the autumn of 1920.

sources.quote: already in the autumn of 1920, when the Institute bullding was nearing completion, Rutherford found time to visit US in Copenhagen

label: Cockcroft and Walton produced alpha particles by proton impact
description: Production of high-speed alpha-particles by proton impact on lithium nuclei was obtained.

sources.quote: production of high-speed a-particles by proton impact on lithium nuclei was obtained in March 1932.

label: Chadwick discovered the neutron
description: Chadwick was able to prove that one was faced with momentum and energy exchanges through a neutral particle.

sources.quote: Chadwick was able to prove that one was faced with momentum and energy exchanges through a neutral particle, the mass of which he determined as differing from that of the proton by less than one part in a thousand.
Less than two years after Rutherford's death in 1937

label: Rutherford was buried in Westminster Abbey
description: Rutherford was buried in Westminster Abbey, close to the sarcophagus of Newton.

sources.quote: On one of the following days, Rutherford was buried in Westminster Abbey, close to the sarcophagus of Newton.

label: Bohr delivered Rutherford Memorial Lecture
description: Bohr delivered the lecture at a meeting of The Physical Society of London.

sources.quote: lecture delivered @lthout a prepared manuscript at a meeting of The Physical Society of London at the Impend College of Science and Technology on 28th November 1958.
